what_happened: After taking over at 4.7 s, the policy left the recorded path, which kept to its lane and bent right. Instead it steered steadily left across the leftmost lane and the shoulder line, and drove into the median guardrail at about 5 m/s by 8.0 s, even though the route command was RIGHT. The camera view was clean while it drifted. No actor was involved: the flagged contact is with the barrier, since all the actor-collision metrics read 0.

The route said LEFT, and the ego crept forward in a stopped queue while edging left toward the gap between actor 21 (directly ahead) and actor 24 (in the left lane). It closed the gap from 10 m to 4.5 m at about 3 m/s and barely slowed, then hit 21's rear-left with its front. The lead car stayed clearly visible in the camera even as the rendering smeared, so the rear contact from 23 came after the front hit, which was the policy's fault.

On the highway at about 41 m/s with a STRAIGHT command, the ego drifted left onto the lane line, toward where the recorded human changed lanes. It was still closing on the white SUV (actor 5) in the left lane, and its front clipped that SUV's rear corner at 6.9 s. The run was also flagged offroad and rear-ended; the rear contact likely came from a replayed actor, after the frontal collision had already begun.

With a RIGHT command, the ego ended up in the leftmost lane, about 10 m left of the recorded path, which heads right. It slowed from 7.8 to 2.2 m/s but kept angling left toward the strip-mall side and crossed the left road edge at 11.2 s. The camera smearing comes from being so far off the recording; it is not a clear cause, since the ego was already off course in the first frame.

After handoff on a multi-lane highway, the ego braked hard for no clear reason (21 → 8 m/s), while the recorded human kept speed and moved left. The ego's plan also drifted right, against a LEFT command, into the lane of semi truck 5, which was passing on its right; the ego's front corner hit the truck's side or rear (front collision at 8.0 s, 4.7 m off the recorded path).

The route command switched from STRAIGHT to RIGHT, and the route bent toward a right-turn lane. The ego slowed from about 24 to 16 m/s but kept heading straight instead of following it, and at 7.2 s it ran into the non-drivable gore area between the through lanes and the right-turn lane, about 5 m off the recorded path. No other actor was close, and the camera view was clean before the failure.

The command switched to RIGHT, and the recorded path bears right where the road splits around a median island. The ego instead held a slightly left-of-centre line and steered into the curbed median gore, going off-road at 7.0 s at about 12 m/s, 4.1 m from the recorded path. No other actors were close, and the camera view was clean before the failure.

The ego stayed at about 41 m/s on the highway, running about 27 m ahead of where the human was at that point in the recording. It then edged left along the human's lane-change path toward the left lane and struck the white SUV (actor 5) in that lane with its front, swerving back right only at the last moment. The flagged off-road and rear contact came after this front collision.

On the highway at about 41 m/s, the ego drifted left out of its lane and into the lane of slower actor 5, never slowing down, and its front hit that car's rear right corner at 6.9s. The recorded human made a similar move left but was about 27 m further back, so it was behind actor 5. The ego was ahead of that position, and its planned path only swung back right at the moment of impact.

On a multi-lane highway that bends left, the ego braked hard (from 19.6 to 7.7 m/s) and kept heading straight instead of following the lanes. That put it across the right lane line into the lane of semi truck 5, which was passing on the right, and the ego's front struck the truck's side about 4.8 m right of the recorded human path, even though the route command was LEFT. The camera smear at impact is just the truck being too close to render; earlier frames were clean.

After handoff the ego braked hard (20 → 8 m/s) and steered right toward the slower semi-truck (actor 5) in the next lane, even though the recorded human path and the LEFT command both went left. The ego's front ran into the rear-left of the truck as it merged into that lane.

The route said RIGHT and the recorded path went ahead and to the right. Instead, the policy steered left at about 6 m/s, out of its lane and across the leftmost lane, and ran off the drivable area into the median guardrail. It ended about 7 m from the human's path. The camera view was clean before the drift, and there was no vehicle in the ego's way.

The ego was on a freeway with a RIGHT command. Its planned path curved left across the yellow edge line into the left shoulder, where it ended up against the median guardrail. By 7.9 s it was off the road, about 7 m from the human's trajectory. The camera view was clean before it drifted and there was no actor in its way.

The route command was RIGHT and the route line pulled right, but after handoff the ego braked and steered left across the lanes. Its front hit vehicle 32, which was in the lane to its left, and it ended up heading toward the left road edge, about 7.3 m off the recorded human path.

With a RIGHT route command, the ego was already in the leftmost lane about 10 m left of the recorded path, and it planned and steered further left. Slowing from 8 to 2 m/s, it crossed the left road boundary toward the parking lot and went offroad at 11.2s, with no other actor involved.

The command changed to RIGHT, but the policy ignored it and kept a straight, slightly left path while slowing from about 23 to 16 m/s. The ego drifted left away from the recorded right-hand path (5 m off) and ran onto the nose of the median island, hitting the median sign, so it was flagged offroad.

In slow queued traffic with a LEFT route command, the ego steered left out of its lane, about 5 m off the recorded path, and tried to squeeze between car 21 ahead and car 24 in the left lane. Its front corner hit car 24 at about 2.7 m/s. Car 23 struck the ego's rear only after this.

After the route command switched to RIGHT, the policy kept planning and driving straight instead of bearing right with the route. The ego drifted about 5 m left of the recorded path into the median and U-turn lane area and went off the road at 16.4 m/s. There was no vehicle ahead and the camera view was clean before the failure.

The command changed to RIGHT as the ego approached an intersection, but it kept going straight and drifted left at about 16–18 m/s. It ended up on the median nose between the through and U-turn lanes, 4.9 m from where the human drove, who bore right. No other actors were nearby and the camera view was clean.

The route command changed to RIGHT and the recorded path bore right at the road split, but the policy kept going straight, slowing from about 21 to 17 m/s. It ended up about 5 m from the recorded path, out of the drivable lanes in the gore/median area of the split. There was no actor ahead, and the camera view was clean before the failure.

In slow queued traffic with a LEFT command, the ego left its lane behind actor 21 and squeezed left toward the next lane while still creeping forward at about 3 m/s. Its front hit the car stopped in that lane (actor 24, at the edge of 21), and the gap fell from 11.7 m to 4.6 m. The rear contact from actor 23 came after the front collision.

In slow traffic with a LEFT command, the ego left the recorded path (about 5 m off by the end) and tried to squeeze left out of its lane into the narrow gap between car 24 on its left and car 21 just ahead. It kept rolling at about 2.5–3 m/s while the gap to the nearly stopped car ahead shrank from 11 m to 4.4 m, and its front hit one of those cars (most likely 21). Car 23 behind then touched its rear, but only after the front collision.

In slow queued traffic with a LEFT command, the ego left its lane behind car 21 and edged left toward the next lane, where car 24 was alongside. Moving at about 2.4 m/s and about 5 m off the recorded path, it made front contact between cars 24 and 21 while merging. Something hit its rear afterwards, but the front collision came first.

On a clear, empty road at about 28 m/s, the ego slowed and drifted left instead of following the route right (the command changed to RIGHT and the recorded path bears right). By 7.0 s it was over the yellow edge line on the left and was flagged offroad, 2.1 m from the recorded path.
